decisions.decision: The fix changes what SHIPS, not only what the trail says: the package descriptor must carry the author's language. A trail-only fix is unavailable because there is no change to attribute — spec 055's FR-016 widened the compared set correctly, but its D-3 premise ('identity answers land in the .kps') is false, so the widening found nothing.

Descriptor fields in scope: the language block (author's composed BCP47 tag, language name as display text) plus package name, package description, and keyboard name. welcome.htm / readme.htm language propagation is excluded as a Content-team surface (spec §12, Constitution Article VII).

The pre-instantiation identity stage is attributed by ON-REQUEST re-derivation — two projections of the working copy differing only in one identity value, compared — rather than by reordering the manifest. Keeps 053's one-capture-per-boundary model and 055 FR-021's on-request discipline; the identity stage stays ahead of base selection.

The adapt track's missing package descriptor is GENERATED by the same single writer the copy track uses, not fetched from the base keyboard's repo. Fetching the raw base .kps is what the loader deliberately refuses to do (it references compiled ../build/*.kmx artifacts); re-introducing that would trade one defect for another.
Extract buildKpsContent from the scaffolder into packages/engine/src/package-descriptor/ and add a patch-or-generate entry point both tracks call
decisions.why: FR-005 requires exactly one writer; E-6 is the cost of two paths - the adapt track never calls the scaffolder, so it shipped no descriptor and the version patch no-opped silently
decisions.rejected: Adding a second studio-side writer for the adapt track, or calling scaffold() during projection (a second instantiation, contra Article III)

decisions.decision: Write the descriptor at projection step 3.6 - after the .kmn identity write, before the id-rename pass
decisions.why: The <Files> list derives from the final .kmn, and running before rename means renameFilesInVfs and rewriteKpsFilePaths compose with no new code - rewriteKpsFilePaths deliberately skips non-path-shaped <Name> values, so the author display names survive
decisions.rejected: Writing after the rename (would duplicate step 4 rewrite logic), or writing in serializeWorkingCopy (would desync the OSK preview from the zip, violating FR-004/SC-005)

decisions.decision: The counterfactual is two calls to projectWorkingCopyForOutput with a new pure identityOverride parameter, diffed
decisions.why: FR-010 requires both sides to come from the function that produces the shipped keyboard; an override keeps it one code path differing in one input, and the function already clones the VFS so the store is untouched
decisions.rejected: Extending the gated-off mutate() seam (its writes containment is IRPath-space and structurally cannot address a .kps), or temporarily setIdentity-ing the alternative and restoring (mutating shared state to answer a read-only question)

decisions.decision: Add a third ImpactUnavailableReason, no-working-copy-yet, with its zod mirror in the same commit
decisions.why: FR-012 requires this state to be distinguishable from the two existing reasons and from changed-nothing; after the fix, no-rederivable-write-path would be a false statement for identity entries
decisions.rejected: Reusing no-rederivable-write-path, or returning null (null already means shed entry and renders a different, wrong notice)

decisions.decision: Impact resolution goes async only where a counterfactual is needed; stored captures stay synchronous, via a useEntryImpact(entry, expanded) hook
decisions.why: The projection is async (it pre-loads patterns), but a stored capture must be returned verbatim per SC-005 and would otherwise flicker through a pending state; keying the effect on expanded preserves FR-011 by construction
decisions.rejected: Making the whole resolver async, or precomputing identity counterfactuals at instantiation (the batch form FR-011 and 053 FR-010 both forbid)

decisions.decision: FR-016 lands as a registry-wide vitest (outputReach.test.ts) with two parts - declaration integrity against a writer-owned field table, plus a curated promise-phrase guard over help_text/prompt
decisions.why: The declarations are TS module exports; the repo already settled this when spec 050 added the tsx-run content-i18n-freshness check because plain-JS content-i18n-lint cannot re-derive from TS-module question definitions. Part (a) alone would pass a question that promises the world and declares outputs: []
decisions.rejected: A new plain-node utilities/ linter (would need its own TypeScript parser), and declaration-integrity-only (does not satisfy SC-008, which is about the promise)

decisions.decision: Declare output reach in a new QuestionModule.outputs field ({target, field}) rather than overloading writes
decisions.why: writes is IRPath[] over KeyboardIR and governs mutate() containment - an identity question declaring writes: [] was always correct. The defect (E-1) was that writes was the only declaration available, so reaching an output file had nowhere to be stated. outputs also tells the counterfactual which overlay field to vary
decisions.rejected: Adding fake IRPaths to writes for identity questions, which would break mutate() containment semantics

decisions.decision: The adapt track descriptor is generated during projection when absent; the loader stays unchanged
decisions.why: fetchKeyboardSourceToVfs deliberately refuses to write the raw .kps because it references compiled ../build/*.kmx artifacts; generating means the <Files> list derives from what this build emits, the same guarantee the copy track has
decisions.rejected: Adding .kps to the loader sibling-fetch filter (re-introduces the compiled-artifact leak), or generating at instantiation (stale the moment identity answers or the .kmn change)

decisions.decision: The feature is numbered 057, matching its git branch; the duplicate specs/058-identity-in-package folder was an artifact of the create-feature script and has been removed
decisions.why: Folder number == branch number is the house convention (053, 055, 056 all hold it), spec.md's own Feature Branch field already said 057, and the plan step summary already called the feature 057. Nothing was committed yet, so the number was still free to correct
decisions.rejected: Keeping 058 and deleting the 057 stub (leaves the folder out of step with the branch, and the extension re-materializes a 057 stub on the next dispatch)

concerns.note: FR-016/SC-008 require a repository check that catches a question promising the author a value no output writer consumes (the E-1/E-4 defect class). The requirement states the outcome; the mechanism — lint over question modules, a test, or a facet check — is a /speckit-plan decision and is deliberately unspecified.

approach: Extract the scaffolder's private buildKpsContent into one engine package-descriptor module with a patch-or-generate entry point, and call it from a new projection step 3.6 (after the .kmn identity write, before the id-rename pass) so both authoring tracks re-derive the descriptor from the same identity overlay. Grow that overlay with the language's English name and, on the copy track, the already-composed BCP47 tag. Attribute the pre-instantiation identity decisions by projecting the working copy twice through projectWorkingCopyForOutput with a pure identityOverride and diffing the two, resolved async on expand only.

plan.summary: Planned 057 at normal size: plan.md with a clean Constitution Check (no violations), research.md with 10 decisions, data-model.md with 6 entities, and 3 contracts (package-descriptor writer, question output-reach declaration + its check, on-request impact resolution). Artifacts were authored under a duplicate specs/058-identity-in-package folder and consolidated into specs/057-identity-in-package to match the branch.
plan.key_finding: The copy track never populates identity.bcp47 at all - it is set only by instantiateFromExisting on the adapt track, while Track 1 writers set just keyboardId and displayName. The composed tag exists in surveySessionStore.identityResult and simply never crosses into the working copy, so the descriptor has no author tag to write even before the writer question is answered.

tasks.summary: 44 tasks across 8 phases: Setup (empty by design), Foundational (the single package-descriptor writer + the outputs declaration), US1 copy-track artifact, US3 adapt-track descriptor, US2 the trail counterfactual, US4 revision, a standalone Anti-regression phase for FR-016/017/018, and Polish. Every phase is laid out as explicit waves with join lines; the widest fan-out is 4.
tasks.key_finding: US3 (P2) is sequenced ahead of US2 (P1), against strict priority order, per the plan sequencing note - US1 and US3 share the writer, and landing US2 before the adapt track has a descriptor would ship the trail attributing a change that exists on only one of the two tracks. The anti-regression work is its own phase rather than Polish because FR-016 check reads the DESCRIPTOR_CONSUMED_FIELDS table the Foundational phase exports, and must see the declarations T005 adds.

FR-001.title: The produced package descriptor MUST declare the author's language, not the base keyboard's, using the tag already composed by the identity-lite series.

FR-002.title: The declared language's display text MUST be the language's name as the author confirmed it, falling back to the tag itself.

FR-003.title: The descriptor's package name, package description, and keyboard name MUST reflect the author's chosen display name.

FR-004.title: FR-001 through FR-003 MUST be satisfied through the single shared output projection; no output path may compute identity independently.

FR-005.title: There MUST be exactly one writer of the package descriptor's identity fields, used by both authoring tracks.

FR-006.title: Both authoring tracks MUST deliver a package descriptor; where one cannot be written, a warning MUST name the failure.

FR-007.title: An optional identity answer left blank MUST leave the descriptor well-formed and buildable, and MUST NOT declare the base keyboard's value.

FR-008.title: The descriptor's keyboard version MUST continue to agree with the keyboard source's version, on both tracks.

FR-009.title: A decision recorded before a working copy exists MUST be resolvable on request by comparing a projection made with the recorded value against one made with the alternative.

FR-010.title: Both sides of that comparison MUST come from the same projection that produces the shipped keyboard.

FR-011.title: The comparison MUST be performed only for the entry the author expanded, and only when they expand it. No batch form, no computation on trail mount.

FR-012.title: Where no working copy exists yet, that MUST be reported as its own reason, distinguishable from the two existing unavailability reasons and from changed-nothing.

FR-013.title: Content that changes on every projection independently of any decision MUST NOT appear in a counterfactual comparison, on either side.

FR-014.title: Where an identity stage resolved several answers, their shared change MUST be attributed jointly; no answer claims it alone.

FR-015.title: Any new author-facing text MUST be added to the studio's own catalog under the established id convention; no English prose in the engine for the author to read.

FR-016.title: Every question whose answer reaches an output file MUST declare that it does, and the mismatch MUST be detectable rather than discovered by reading the artifact.

FR-017.title: A test asserting behaviour of the package descriptor MUST NOT supply the descriptor it is proving exists; coverage MUST include both tracks.

FR-018.title: il_language_code's help-text promise that the code goes on the finished keyboard MUST be true when this feature lands, or the text MUST change.
